document.abstract: A laboratory model of a magnetic-drive film-phonograph was modified so that speed fluctuations of large and measurable magnitude and of frequencies ranging from 1/2 to 7 cycles could be introduced either into the sprocket rotation or the magnet rotation. The resulting speed variations at the drum were determined by means of a “wowmeter.” The large ratios of flutter reduction indicated by these measurements show in part why the magnetic drive gives unsurpassed film motion.
